rv.q: Are You Even Indian, is a gorgeous mix of theatre and dance, exploring whether a British-born Indian woman and Indian-born man can solve clashes over what it means to be Indian.
Are You Even Indian? is a warmly watchable 60 minutes of theatre which raises issues at least two levels.
Every scene is a delight to watch whilst also sparking thought and reflection on the deeper themes of the play.
Are You Even Indian? is a wonderfully perceptive and moving piece of theatre. It captures the nuance of the British Indian experience with warmth and understanding without cliche.
Using mixed media, dance and brilliant writing, Are You Even Indian? is not only a conversation starter but also part of the conversation it seeks to provoke.

Mathur ’s script is insightful, courageously embracing complexity. It looks at the predicament of immigrants with both intellectual sharpness and empathy – the price to pay being that “both your homes ask you to apologise for who you are.”
Are you even Indian? is a compelling story of cultural nuances, perceptions, aspirations, and expectations.

cn.t: Critics praise Mohit Mathur's "Are You Even Indian?" as a witty, poignant exploration of South Asian identity and belonging, blending Bollywood dance with sharp writing. Reception ranges from enthusiastic to warmly positive.
